finding.text: The heal also runs on every `visibilitychange` to visible (`Server/SiteGateway.mjs:200`), so any tab left open across a merge reloads itself the moment the owner comes back to it. On the phone, turning the screen off and on during a voice call (Recite, `/api/voice*` through this gateway) would drop the call and any typed draft after every merge, and merges land many times a day. Keep the reload for the case the brief names, a page that came out of the cache (`load` and `pageshow` with `persisted`), or skip the reload while the mic or a call is live.

The task folder can't be picked up by a fresh agent. `session.jsonl` holds only the assign line and one commit stamp. Nothing records the worktree branch (`worktree/cache-version`), the test result (`node Server/SiteGateway.cache.test.mjs`, 9 steps), whether the gateway was restarted, or that the work is still unmerged. Add a log line or outcome that says these things.

Ask 1 said `git rev-parse --short HEAD`. The build uses `git log -1 --format=%h -- *.js *.mjs *.css *.html *.webmanifest` (`Server/SiteGateway.mjs:165`), so log sweeps and doc commits don't clear every browser. That's a sensible change from the owner's wording, and `tunnel.md` says why, but the report to the owner should name it too (law 4).

`inject()` (`Server/SiteGateway.mjs:204`): a page with no `<head>` gets the script put in front of `<!doctype html>`, which puts that page in quirks mode. Also, `/<head[^>]*>/` also matches `<header>`. Real pages (`public/index.html`) have a `<head>`, so this only reaches stray `.html` fixtures. Inserting after the doctype instead would cover both.

`version()` runs `execFileSync` inside the request path (`Server/SiteGateway.mjs:165`). It blocks the gateway, SSE streams included, once every 30 s. It took 31 ms here, so this is fine for now. A background refresh (`execFile` on a timer) would take it off the request path.

A page response that still arrives compressed skips the clear as well as the heal (`html` requires `!h["content-encoding"]`, `:230-231`). Before this change, the clear did not depend on encoding. `accept-encoding` is dropped upstream (`:221`), so this should never happen. It is still a quiet way for the cookie guard to stop working.

Ask 3 isn't proven any more. The test never holds a stale copy: step 1 loads through the gateway, which now sends `no-store`, so nothing is cached, and step 3 would pass even if `Clear-Site-Data` did nothing. The old "stale copy sticks" step was deleted (`Server/SiteGateway.cache.test.mjs:54-58`). Seed the stale `max-age` copy straight from the fake site (not through the gateway), then load through the gateway with an old cookie and show that v2 runs.

Asks 1 and 2 were replaced by a different design (`no-store` plus a hand-bumped `CACHE_V = "2"`), and only `Servex/ext/remote/doc/tunnel.md:46` says so. The task folder has no line recording the decision, and the owner's report hasn't been written. The owner asked for both by name (law 4), so the report has to say what was built instead and why. The asked-for `"stale code healed"` trace line is gone too, so the phone's log can't prove the fix.

`Servex/ext/remote/doc/tunnel.md:48` says "(numbers just below)", but no numbers follow; the next paragraph is "Later: a real login". Add the measured size of one page's module tree, or cut the phrase.

A fresh agent can't continue from this folder. `session.jsonl` still has only the assign line, the review and commit stamps. Nothing records the branch (`worktree/cache-version`, head `4d9bd2e84`), the test result, that it is unmerged, or whether the gateway was restarted (a `Server/` change needs a restart). The round-1 review asked for exactly this (its finding 2).

`CACHE_V` is a manual bump again (`Server/SiteGateway.mjs:40`), which is the failure the brief opened with. With `no-store` that matters less, but the comment should say when to bump it: only to clear copies that were cached before `no-store`.

`no-store` makes every phone load re-download the whole module tree. It also keeps those pages out of Chrome's back/forward cache, so Back reloads them. The versioned-URL follow-up (`tunnel.md:48`) should be filed as a task on the session, not just mentioned in a doc.
`Server/readme.md` doesn't list `SiteGateway.cache.test.mjs`. That was already true before this change.

`Servex/ext/remote/doc/tunnel.md:48` says "see *Measured through the tunnel* below", but there is no such section (grep finds only line 48 itself). Either measure the load through the tunnel and add the numbers, or cut the pointer and say that measurement is still to do.

The design change that replaced asks 1 and 2 ("Plan A, 13:25 change from vscode-mastermind", `session.jsonl:9`) isn't recorded anywhere a fresh agent can read it: it's not in `inbox.jsonl` or `requirements.md`, and it has no link to its source. Add the instruction, or a link to it, to the task folder so the reason it's no longer the owner's brief can be traced.

The `B` follow-up (an import map to versioned `immutable` URLs, `tunnel.md:48`) and "restart the gateway (found down, 502)" exist only as "Next:" in a log line (`session.jsonl:9`). File them as tasks on the session (law 10, "file each ask") so they survive if this agent stops before it merges.

The test now proves the clear really evicts a stuck copy, but it uses `/stale.png` as a stand-in (`Server/SiteGateway.cache.test.mjs:20`). A stuck `.js` can't be seeded through the gateway any more, since it sends `no-store`. That's a fair proxy for ask 3, but the test's header comment should say the png stands in for the phone's stuck `Recite.js`. Step 1's label still says "seed", even though nothing is cached at that step.

`no-store` on HTML keeps every page out of Chrome's back/forward cache, and every phone load downloads the whole module tree again (873 requests, `tunnel.md:48`). That's acceptable for a dev-tunnel site, but it's the cost to weigh when deciding on B.
`CACHE_V = "2"` (`Server/SiteGateway.mjs:40`) is still bumped by hand, the failure the brief opened with. The new comment says when to bump it, which is enough now that code goes out `no-store`.
